alert.raw: HIGH: Impossible travel detected. User m.johnson authenticated from New York, USA at 09:02:14Z then Tokyo, Japan at 09:14:52Z — 12 minutes 38 seconds apart, 10,840 km distance. Both sessions passed MFA. Post-login bulk CRM and SharePoint data access observed.

telemetry.detail: m.johnson login from 73.45.22.190 (Verizon FiOS residential, New York, NY, US). MFA: TOTP app approved. Device: MacBook Pro 14, Chrome 126, fingerprint matches 47 prior logins.
m.johnson login from 42.112.88.31 (NTT residential, Tokyo, Japan). MFA: TOTP app approved. Device: Windows 11, Edge 126 — NEW DEVICE, not in trusted device registry.
Distance: 10,840 km. Elapsed: 762 seconds. Required speed: 51,227 km/h. Minimum commercial flight: ~13.5 hours. Physically impossible without VPN/proxy.
GET /services/data/v59.0/query?q=SELECT+Id,Name,Email,Phone,AnnualRevenue+FROM+Account+LIMIT+2500 — 2,441 records returned. Anomalous: m.johnson's baseline max export is 50 records.
15 files downloaded: Q3 Sales Forecast.xlsx, Customer Pipeline 2026.xlsx, Product Roadmap CONFIDENTIAL.pptx, Pricing Strategy H2.xlsx, and 11 others. Total: 847 MB.
New York session (MacBook/Chrome): active, browsing intranet. Tokyo session (Windows/Edge): still active, no logout. Concurrent sessions from two continents.

cachedVerdict.reasoning: Impossible travel is confirmed — the physics are irreconcilable. However, automated escalation to confirmed account compromise requires human judgment: (1) Both sessions passed TOTP MFA, which requires either physical access to the authenticator app or a real-time AiTM (adversary-in-the-middle) phishing attack that relays TOTP codes. TOTP relaying is technically feasible and increasingly common. (2) The Tokyo session uses a new, unregistered device fingerprint (Windows/Edge vs. m.johnson's Mac/Chrome baseline) — a VPN exit node would not change the device fingerprint, making VPN the less likely explanation. (3) Bulk CRM export (2,441 records vs. 50-record baseline) and 15 confidential SharePoint files within 60 seconds of login is highly anomalous and matches data theft behavior regardless of whether the account is compromised. The correct action is to contact m.johnson on a verified out-of-band channel immediately, terminate the Tokyo session proactively, and initiate a DLP review of accessed data.

cachedVerdict.ciso_summary: One of our employee accounts appears to have been accessed simultaneously from New York and Tokyo within 13 minutes — a physical impossibility — and during the Tokyo session someone bulk-downloaded thousands of customer records and confidential business documents including our sales forecast and pricing strategy. We have already terminated the suspicious session and are contacting the employee directly to confirm whether they authorized this access, which will determine our next steps. If confirmed as unauthorized, we may be required to notify affected customers about the data that was accessed.
cachedVerdict.summary: Impossible travel: NY→Tokyo in 12m38s with new device fingerprint; Tokyo session bulk-accessed 2,441 CRM records and 15 confidential files. MFA passed both sessions. Contact user immediately; terminate Tokyo session proactively pending verification.
